note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BAH 9, Schedule 2-3; A06b BAH 9, Schedule 2-3; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 7 years' residence (the 12 months before the application and 6 of the 9 years before them; the dataset's own count is 6); the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Wedlock restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a wedlock restriction (a child born out of wedlock may not take it from a citizen father), which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Bahamas, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in the Bahamas for 12 months immediately prior to the application, and was either resident in the country, in the service of the government, or had partly such residence and partly such service for 6 out of 9 years prior to the 12-month period and intent to make the Bahamas his/her permanent home (either by residence or government service). ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... n.a. ... Wedlock restriction ... Person is born in the Bahamas to a citizen parent in wedlock or to a citizen mother out of wedlock. ... Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply) ... Person is born abroad to a father who himself is a citizen otherwise than by mode A01b.; Person is born abroad to a mother who is a citizen married to a foreigner or to a citizen mother who is not married to the foreign father, and registers between the age of 18 and 21. Other conditions: renunciation of another citizenship (unless this is legally impossible), and oath of allegiance. Registration can be denied in the interests of national security or public policy, or if the person within a period of 5 years immediately preceding the application was sentenced to death or a prison sentence of at least 12 months, is not of good behaviour, is a danger to public safety, has been declared bankrupt, or has insufficient means to support him/herself. ... No provision ... No provision

Other conditions: renunciation of another citizenship (unless this is legally impossible), and oath of allegiance. Registration can be denied in the interests of national security or public policy, or if the person within a period of 5 years immediately preceding the application was sentenced to death or a prison sentence of at least 12 months, is not of good behaviour, is a danger to public safety, has been declared bankrupt, or has insufficient means to support him/herself.
